newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metal futures extend losses.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metal futures extend losses.

text.p: Tokyo precious metal futures extended early losses to end lower on Tuesday, pressured by private investors' long-liquidation and a further drop in spot precious metal prices, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from seven to 11 yen per gram lower, with benchmark August finishing 11 yen down at 1,332 yen.
Market sentiment in Tokyo was overwhelmingly bearish.

"Despite the yen's recent weakness against the dollar, there had been little buying interest. The market looks more responsive to bearish factors rather than bullish factors," an analyst at a commodity broker said.
The analyst said private investors could sell aggressively if the yen gains against the dollar.
Spot gold extended losses during Asian hours, quoted at $377.60/90 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against the close in New York of $378.20/60 and London's fix at $379 on Monday.

Traders also said that massive long positions in platinum and gold futures still held by private investors weighed on the market, adding they were especially long in the December platinum contract. They said spot gold could test support at $375 while platinum could break under $380 per ounce.
Platinum futures ranged from five to 13 yen per gram lower.
Benchmark August hit its life-of-contract low at the close, down 13 yen at 1,349 yen.
Spot platinum was quoted at $381.00/381.75 at the Tokyo close, after opening at $382.25/383.00.
Japanese traders said Japan's weak demand for platinum group metals discouraged buying interest even after prices fell.
Silver futures ranged from 0.9 yen to 2.2 yen per 10 grams lower, with benchmark August ending 1.2 yen lower at 175.9.
Palladium was mixed. Key August was down one yen at 422.
